All quotes verbatim from the clone at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-bsd-seed-lab/ab9d3026-f88f-51d1-8e47-f94a5d2c0e6f/scratchpad/openai_math_clone/repo/preprints/ (commit fd4aeeb2). Grade of every statement: IMPORTED_PREPRINT (unrefereed, AI-generated, no Lean for the BSD family).

(1) ExactBSD = Exact-Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer-Formula-from-Low-Selmer-Corank-October-7-2026/build/sections/.
 Standing setting, 06-pair.tex:3-9: "Fix an odd prime \(p\). We retain the imaginary quadratic field \(K\), the auxiliary field \(L\), and the tuple of tame directions constructed in Sections 2 and 4. Thus \(p=w\bar w\) in \(K\), every rational prime below the fixed finite support for \(E/K\) splits in \(K\), and \(R=\Z_p[[t,u_1,\ldots,u_d]]\) has one genuine anticyclotomic variable \(t\)."
 The field K comes from Lemma 2.6 (classical:auxiliary-fields), 02-classical.tex:117-139: "Let $E/\Q$ have conductor $N$ and analytic rank $r\in\{0,1\}$. There exist coprime negative odd fundamental discriminants $D,D'<-4$ such that, for $K=\Q(\sqrt D)$, $F=\Q(\sqrt{DD'})$, $L=\Q(\sqrt D,\sqrt{D'})$, the following statements hold. (i) Every prime dividing $2Np$ splits in both imaginary quadratic fields, and $(D/|D'|)=1$. (ii) The analytic ranks of $E^D,E^{D'},E^{DD'}$ are respectively $1-r,1-r,r$. (iii) The extension $L/F$ is CM and unramified at every finite place, and $L$ has only the roots of unity $\{\pm1\}$. (iv) One may require $L\cap\Q(E[p])=\Q$ ... Both $L(E/K,s)$ and $L(E^{D'}/K,s)$ have a simple zero at $s=1$." Its proof uses Theorem 2.5 (classical:twist-density, 02-classical.tex:103-109): "For every elliptic curve $A/\Q$, among nonzero squarefree integers $d$ ordered by $|d|$, the twists $A^d$ of analytic rank zero and one each have density $1/2$." with "We use the theorem at the scope stated in \cite[Theorem~1.2]{Goldfeld}" — references.tex:143-147 shows {Goldfeld} = OpenAI, 'Goldfeld's analytic density conjecture and the 2-converse for elliptic curves' (an OAI manuscript, i.e. Goldfeld's CONJECTURE is imported as a theorem from an unrefereed AI preprint). 02-classical.tex:186-193: "For the rest of the pair construction, fix such $D,D',K,F,L$ ... The rational compact Selmer group over $K$ for each of $E,E'$ has dimension one." Theorem 2.7 (classical:gross-zagier), 02-classical.tex:228-241: "With the preceding conventions, $D$ odd fundamental, $(D,N)=1$, all level primes split, and $\mathcal O_K^\times=\{\pm1\}$, one has [GZ formulas] ... In the simple-zero case $P_K$ is nontorsion." (imported Gross–Zagier 1986).
 Proposition 6.6 (pair:finite-divisibility), 06-pair.tex:653-663: "For every sufficiently high finite \(\theta\), $B_w(\theta,\mathbf u)\in L_w(\theta,\mathbf u)A_\theta'$. (15) With the same global character variable, the two nonzero quotients for \(w\) and \(\bar w\) are associates in \(A_\theta'\)."
 Lemma 6.8 (pair:derivatives, 'Inert derivative coordinates'), 06-pair.tex:846-866: "There are fresh inert good prime sequences \(\ell\), with \(\ell\to-1\) and Tate Frobenius tending to \(J=\rho_T(\tau)\) for complex conjugation \(\tau\), for which the limiting local degree-one cohomology splits into finite and transverse planes. ... These classes satisfy $f_{\rm loc}(Z_{I\cup\ell})=0$, $s_{\rm loc}(Z_{I\cup\ell})=Jf_{\rm loc}(Z_I)$." (proof 'following \cite[Section~9, Inert derivative identity, equation (K)]{B}', i.e. the OAI TwoPrimary manuscript.)
 Corollary 6.9 (pair:integral-quotient), 06-pair.tex:1048-1057: "Using the descended analytic ideals, the fraction $U_w=B_w/L_w$ is represented by an integral series, and \(p\nmid U_w\). Removing any newly added tame variables specializes it to the old quotient times an integral unit. This includes removal of all tame variables, leaving the genuine anticyclotomic line."
 Proposition 8.1 (extraction:theta-implication), 08-extraction.tex:28-42: "Let $\mathfrak p$ be a horizontal height-one prime of the deformation ring, with the auxiliary tuple conditions of Section 7. If $b_w^0\in\mathfrak p$, then, over $\Frac(R/\mathfrak p)$, at least one of $H^1_{\mathrm{prim},a}(K,V\chi)$, $H^1_{\mathrm{prim},a}(K,V'\chi)$ is nonzero. Here $a$ is one fixed side determined by the reciprocity convention of Section 7. ..."
 Theorem 9.6 (unit:unit-comparison), 09-unit.tex:396-401: "The two quotients $U_w$ are units. Their specialization with all artificial variables zero gives an integral unit comparison between the analytic series and strict determinant on the true anticyclotomic line." Proof 09-unit.tex:403-449 cites Prop 9.5 (unit:simultaneous-jumps, 09-unit.tex:252-266: "The new tame directions can be chosen so that, for every such $\mathfrak q$, the following two loci have codimension at least two in $\Spec S_{(\mathfrak q,\mathbf y)}$: 1. the locus where both one-sided primitive complexes for a single representation jump; 2. for each allocation of sides, the locus where one one-sided primitive complex for each of $V_0,V_1$ jumps."), Cor 6.9, Lemma 9.1 (unit:quotient-regularity, 09-unit.tex:38-49: "... Every irreducible divisor of either $U_w$ is horizontal and has nonzero reduction modulo $(p,t)$."), the 'two conjugate theta implications' (Prop 8.1) and eq. (17).
 Proposition 10.1 (center:exact-factor), 10-center.tex:34-54, in the setting 10-center.tex:11-18 "Put $K=\Q(\sqrt D)$ as in Lemma 2.6 ... The group $E(K)$ has rank one and $\Sha(E/K)$ is finite": "$-v_p(L_w^{s=1}(0)) = d(C_w^{s=1}(0),1) = 2n_P+2\tau_g-s_K-2(v_p(\log_{\omega_E}P_K)-l+\tau_p)-2\sum_{q\in S^\circ}\tau_q$ (22). Consequently $2(n_P+\tau_g)=s_K+2v_p(c_E)+2\sum_q v_p(c_q(E))$ (23)." Corollary 10.2 (center:pair-discrepancy), 10-center.tex:143-150: "For every elliptic curve of analytic rank zero or one, including CM curves, and for the imaginary twist in Lemma 2.6, $X(E)+X(E^D)=0$. (24)"

(2) TwoPrimary = The-two-primary-Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer-formula-in-Selmer-corank-at-most-one-October-6-2026/build/sections/. Proposition 8.1 (split-measures:reducible-input), 08-split-measures.tex:10-22: "Let \(E/\mathbb Q\) be a non-CM elliptic curve with \(E(\mathbb Q)[2]\ne0\), and put \(N=\mathrm{cond}(E)\). Let \(d\equiv7\pmod{16}\) be prime and suppose that every prime dividing \(2N\) splits in \(K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-d})\). If \(s_2(E/K)=1\), then \(L(E/K,s)=L(E,s)L(E^{-d},s)\) has a simple zero at \(1\), and $X(E)+X(E^{-d})=0$. If the product is already known to have a simple zero at \(1\), the same valuation identity holds without separately assuming the Selmer corank condition." Lemma 9.5 (split-local:inert-planes), 09-split-local.tex:145-150: "At an auxiliary inert prime satisfying the preceding full-Tate approximation conditions, the limiting local complex has split free cohomology $M, M\oplus M, M$ in degrees 0,1,2. ... Their mixed pairing is, up to a unit, \(\langle x,Jy\rangle\) ..." (approximation conditions 09-split-local.tex:136-141: fresh rational primes \(\ell\) inert in \(K\) with \(\ell\to-1, a_\ell\to0, \rho(\gamma)\to J, J^2=1\), 2-adically). Proposition 9.7 (split-local:derivative, 'Inert derivative identity'), 09-split-local.tex:203-219: "... at a newly switched prime \(\ell\notin I\) one has $s_{\rm loc}(Z_{I\cup\{\ell\}})=J f_{\rm loc}(Z_I)$, $f_{\rm loc}(Z_{I\cup\{\ell\}})=0$, (K) and the transverse condition in the second identity holds at every switched prime." Proposition 9.13 (split-local:heegner-rank), 09-split-local.tex:441-460: "Let \(f\) be a normalized primitive weight-two newform of trivial nebentypus and level \(N_f\) ... Let \(K\) have odd fundamental discriminant \(-D<-4\), prime to \(N_f\), and suppose every prime dividing \(N_f\) splits in \(K\). ... \(F_f\) a finite extension of \(\mathbb Q_2\) ... Assume \(V_f|_{G_K}\) absolutely irreducible. Then $L(f/K,s)$ has a simple zero at 1 $\Longrightarrow H^1_f(K,V_f)=F_f y, y\ne0, \tau y=-w(f)y$ (K0) ..." Lemma 12.1 (alternation-imaginary:alternation), 12-alternation-imaginary.tex: "With the coefficient module, local conditions, and isotropy data just specified, let \(s\in R\) be a regular scalar. On degree one for coefficients mod \(s\), with \(\partial\) the Bockstein from mod \(s^2\), one has $\langle x,\partial x\rangle=0$. (H1)" Corollary 12.2: "For a perfect two-term DVR complex in degrees \(1,2\) with perfect self-duality of shift \(-3\), arising from the preceding local conditions and satisfying (H1), the generic and special first-cohomology dimensions have the same parity."

(3) Goldfeld2 = Goldfelds-analytic-density-conjecture-and-the-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-October-7-2026/build/sections/. Standing Heegner conditions 01-arithmetic-transfer.tex:112-114: "Let $K=\Q(\sqrt{k})$, where $k<0$ is an odd fundamental discriminant and every prime dividing $2N$ splits in $K$. We omit the two fields with extra units and, if $E$ has complex multiplication, its CM field." Theorem 3.3 (thm:heegner-interpolation), 01-arithmetic-transfer.tex:179-205: "Fix $E$ and an initial discriminant $h_0$. Consider families $h_x$, $x\in\F_2^b$ ... For each family let $k$ define an imaginary field satisfying the standing Heegner conditions ... Assume this base Selmer group has corank one. Suppose, for every $x\ne0$, the product $L(E^{(h_x)},s)L(E^{(h_xk)},s)$ has a simple zero and $2j(P_{|h_x|}(h_x))-4w(h_x)-s(h_x)-s(h_xk)\le B$. Then, for sufficiently large $b$, the base product has a simple zero." Theorem 3.7 (thm:heegner-ring-bound), 01-arithmetic-transfer.tex:284-294: "In ring data, suppose the product in Equation (3.1) has a simple zero, every $q\mid h$ splits in $K$, and $\omega(k)\le a$ ... Then $2j(P_{|h|}(h))\ge 4w(h)+s(h)+s(hk)-O_{E,a}(1)$. There is no irreducibility assumption on $E[2]$." Lemma 13.12 (rd:derivative / lem:h:derivative-classes, 'Descent and the switch at 2'), 03-heegner.tex:1126-1140: "... There is one integer \(L\ne0\), depending on the fixed curve, parametrization and fixed local types, such that the classes obtained from the Heegner derivatives of \(L\) times the point satisfy, for every finite switched set \(I\), $P_I\in H^1(C_I)$, $f(P_{I\cup\{\ell\}})=0$, $s(P_{I\cup\{\ell\}})=C_\tau f(P_I)$." (proof ends 03-heegner.tex:1420-1424: "The displayed local formulas agree with the calculation underlying \cite[Proposition~1.7.4]{Howard2012}; Howard's odd-prime global hypotheses are not being asserted at \(2\).")

(4) Pointwise2 = A-pointwise-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-with-rational-two-torsion-October-7-2026/build/sections/. Standing exclusions ring-limits.tex:13-16: "The imaginary quadratic field $K=\mathbf Q(\sqrt k)$ satisfies the split Heegner hypothesis at $2N$. We omit the two fields with extra units and, when $E$ has complex multiplication, its CM field." Theorem 4.2 (rd:missing-vertex), ring-limits.tex:64-89: "Fix the ring data \(E,K\), with $\operatorname{corank}_{\mathbb Z_2}\operatorname{Sel}_{2^\infty}(E/K)=1$. Suppose binary families exist for arbitrarily large \(b\), and for every nonzero \(x\) the product \(L(E^{(h_x)},s)L(E^{(h_xk)},s)\) has a simple zero and $2j_{h_x}-4w(h_x)-s(h_x)-s(h_xk)\le B$ ... Then $\operatorname{ord}_{s=1}(L(E,s)L(E^{(k)},s))=1$." Lemma 5.2 (rd:derivative), ring-determinants.tex:182-199: same switch identity as Goldfeld2 Lemma 13.12 with $s(P_{I\cup\{\ell\}})=J f(P_I)$, 'We use Kolyvagin's derivative operators \cite{Kolyvagin1990}, keeping their integral descent explicit at $2$.' Proposition 5.10 (rd:central-formula), ring-determinants.tex:980-1003: "Suppose the product $L(E^{(h)},s)L(E^{(hk)},s)$ has a simple zero at \(s=1\). ... $v(u_h(0)) = 2j_h-\operatorname{length}_{\mathbb Z_2}\Sha(E^{(h)}/K)[2^\infty]-2\sum_{p\mid h}t_p+O_E(1) = 2j_h-s(h)-s(hk)-4w(h)+O_{E,A}(1)$."

(5) SelmerConverse = The-Selmer-converse-for-elliptic-curves-at-every-prime-October-7-2026/build/sections/. Field choice Lemma 2.x (lem:auxiliary-fields), 02-reduction.tex:78-92: "There are coprime negative odd fundamental discriminants $D,D'$ such that every prime dividing $2Np$ splits in both quadratic fields ..."; 02-reduction.tex:177-178: "Every prime dividing $N$ splits in $K$, so the classical Heegner hypothesis holds."; 02-reduction.tex:191-194 contradiction hypothesis "$y=0$ in $A_0(K)\otimes\Q$". Proposition 3.7 (prop:heegner-log), 03-tame-deformation.tex:746-760: "At the distinguished place over $p$, and for either sign, $\sum_{g\in\mathcal G_i}(1+t)^{\pm\ell_i(g)}\log_{A_0,p}(y_i^g)\longrightarrow0\pmod{t^{b_*}}$. More precisely, every coefficient of degree less than $b_*$ has valuation tending to $+\infty$ along $\cU$. ..." Equation (katz-abelian-log), 05-constant-terms.tex:315-321: "$F_0(x)=\kappa^{-1}\sum_r e_rp^{-r}\log_{A_0,p}(\varphi(\mathrm{Fr}^{r}x))$", with 05-constant-terms.tex:224-228 "The passage from raised CM values to a Heegner logarithm follows the $p$-adic period method of BDP ... Their construction is made under $p\nmid N$. We give the primitive and logarithm comparison for the reduction types occurring here." and :251 "even when $p\mid N$" — always with $p$ SPLIT in $K$ (02-reduction.tex:205-207: "All the fields introduced above are split at $p$").

Lab target for comparison (work/plectic_step2_return_2026-09-30/RETURN.md): "TH (5843). There exist k ≥ 1 and a k-admissible prime ℓ (FG25 §3.1) such that the linear coefficient c_1(λ_ℓ) of FG25's level-raised theta element λ_ℓ ∈ Λ/p^kΛ (Def 3.14; Gross points on the definite algebra of discriminant ℓ·3·2243, Eichler level 5843·2^3·4547^2) at the trivial character is nonzero in Z/p^k." and FG25 Remark 3.5 (FG25_ACCESS_AND_THM34.md): converse of Thm 3.4 needs "full Heegner point MC in this setting; BCK's approach needs anticyclotomic p-adic L-functions nonzero mod p at the trivial character, which acquire an exceptional zero when p is multiplicative ([CH18, Thm A])."
hypotheses_check:
Common hypotheses of every statement in (1)-(5): (H1) classical Heegner hypothesis — every prime dividing N (and 2, and p) SPLITS in K; (H2) p = w·w̄ SPLIT in K (ExactBSD §6-10, SelmerConverse; TwoPrimary/Goldfeld2/Pointwise2 are p = 2 with 2 split); (H3) E/K of rank one with finite Ш, equivalently analytic rank of E in {0,1} and simple zero of L(E/K,s) (ExactBSD Lemma 2.6, Prop 6.6 setting, Prop 10.1; TwoPrimary Prop 8.1 's_2(E/K)=1', Prop 9.13 'simple zero'; Goldfeld2 Thm 3.3 'base Selmer group has corank one', Thm 3.7 'simple zero'; Pointwise2 Thm 4.2 'corank 1', Prop 5.10 'simple zero'; SelmerConverse Prop 3.7 lives inside a contradiction argument whose outer hypothesis is corank r in {0,1}); (H4) p odd for ExactBSD; p = 2 and E(Q)[2] != 0 for TwoPrimary §8-9, Pointwise2; (H5) O_K^x = {±1}, K not the CM field.

The lab's anticyclotomic setting (reference/07_good_primes.tex:23: 'K = Q(sqrt-7) ... The primes 3, 2243, 5843 are inert in K, which puts us in the definite setting of Bertolini–Longo–Venerucci with N^- = 3·2243·5843 and N^+ = 2^3·4547^2'; plectic route: FG25 with p = 5843 inert, N^- = 3·2243): rank E(K) = 2 with (r+, r−) = (2, 0) (SEED_CONTEXT line 39), ord_{s=1} L(E/K,s) >= 2.

Prime by prime, for E over K = Q(sqrt-7):
- p = 2 (I1* additive, c_2 = 2): 2 splits in K (H2 ok) but ExactBSD requires p odd (H4 fails); TwoPrimary/Goldfeld2/Pointwise2 are the right prime but need (H1): fails since 3, 2243, 5843 are inert in K; (H3) fails: s_2(E/K) = s_2(E) + s_2(E^{-7}) = 2 + 0 = 2 (Ш[2^∞](E) = 0, rank 2; E^{-7} corank 0). TwoPrimary Prop 8.1 also needs d ≡ 7 mod 16 prime: d = 7 ok, E(Q)[2] = Z/2 ok, non-CM ok — but the Heegner and corank conditions fail. Obligation at 2 is anyway closed (Ш[2^∞] = 0).
- p = 3 (I2 nonsplit multiplicative): 3 is INERT in K — (H1) and (H2) both fail. (H3) fails (rank 2). Obligation closed anyway (Ш[3^∞] ≅ (Z/3)^2 PROVED).
- p = 2243 (I1 split multiplicative; ρ̄ ⊇ SL2 recorded): 2243 INERT in K — (H1), (H2) fail; (H3) fails. Also K-2243 (KILL_TESTS_TH.md): Q_K(2243) = 0 is a theorem, so the plectic route is dead at 2243 regardless.
- p = 4547 (type III additive, pot. supersingular; ρ̄ image NOT recorded): 4547 splits in K, so (H2) would hold for ExactBSD, but (H1) fails (3, 2243, 5843 inert) and (H3) fails (rank 2). No manuscript statement covers an additive prime in the anticyclotomic argument anyway (ExactBSD 06-pair.tex:71-77 claims only 'including the case p | N' for the ordinary-locus primitive, with p split in K).
- p = 5843 (I2 nonsplit multiplicative, a_p = −1; ρ̄ ⊇ SL2 recorded; FG25 Ass 1.1/1.2 verified by the lab): 5843 INERT in K — (H1), (H2) fail; (H3) fails. This is exactly the definite / exceptional-zero configuration (FG25 Rem 3.5) and NO manuscript in the repository contains a statement with p inert in K (repo-wide grep for anticyclotomic: only the 3 BSD manuscripts + their earlier versions, all with p split; grep for 'bipartite', 'Jochnowitz' (only a Hecke-algebra paper cites Jochnowitz82), 'exceptional zero' (0 hits in the BSD family), 'level raising' (TwoPrimary 14-cyclic.tex:106 only, at split data), 'Bertolini–Darmon 2005', 'Longo', 'Venerucci', 'Chida–Hsieh', 'Burungale–Castella–Kim', 'Skinner–Zhang': 0 hits). The only inert primes in any manuscript are AUXILIARY Kolyvagin-derivative primes ℓ (ExactBSD Lemma 6.8, TwoPrimary Prop 9.7, Goldfeld2 Lemma 13.12, Pointwise2 Lemma 5.2), never p itself.
- Good ordinary p ≥ 5 (K-route, reference/07_good_primes.tex Thm B.3/B.5): for p with (−7/p) = 1 (H2) holds, for (−7/p) = −1 it fails; in both cases (H1) fails (3, 2243, 5843 inert in K) and (H3) fails (rank E(K) = 2). The lab's frozen route needs BLV Thm 7.3 (char ideal = (F F^ι)) on the DEFINITE side (Gross points on the quaternion algebra ramified at {3, 2243, 5843, ∞}); ExactBSD Thm 9.6 concerns the INDEFINITE/BDP-type measure B_w built from the modular parametrization X_0(N) → E and Heegner points (06-pair.tex:28-33, 10-center.tex:11-18). Different objects; no manuscript compares them.
- Good supersingular p (23, 29, ..., 1823): same failures; additionally ExactBSD never uses p-ordinarity but TwoPrimary §9 / Goldfeld2 / Pointwise2 are p = 2 only.
- ρ̄_p surjectivity: ExactBSD claims no residual hypothesis (06-pair.tex:38-49 uses only Serre open image); the lab records ρ̄ ⊇ SL2(F_p) only at p ∈ {2243, 5843}; irrelevant here since the hypotheses above already fail.

For E^{-7} (rank 0, L(E^{-7},1) ≠ 0, conductor 49N): (H3) holds with r = 0 and a FRESH auxiliary K' (split at 2·49N·p, Lemma 2.6) — this is the ExactBSD-thm:main-for-the-twist item, ALREADY COVERED by assess/twist-E-7.json (CONDITIONALLY_USEFUL, grade IMPORTED_PREPRINT) and assess/chain-provenance.json (NOT_USABLE for any live route). It is NOT the present candidate: the plectic obstacle (lemma TH), FG Thm 3.4's converse and BLV's equality live over K = Q(sqrt-7) for E, not over an auxiliary K' for E^{-7}; nothing about E^{-7} over K' feeds Q_K, λ_ℓ or BLV's F. K-RANK2 applied: every statement here needs corank ≤ 1 over K; for E, corank Sel_{p^∞}(E/K) ≥ 2 at every p (rank 2 + Kummer injection), so none applies to E over any imaginary quadratic field, including a hypothetical K' in which 5843 splits (switching K would also destroy FG's p-inert plectic setup).
deduction_for_seed:
No chain exists. The three attempted chains and the exact break:

Chain A (lemma TH directly): want k ≥ 1, k-admissible ℓ (ℓ ∤ N inert in K = Q(sqrt-7), ℓ² ≢ 1 mod 5843, E[p^k] split at ℓ) with c_1(λ_ℓ) ≠ 0 in Z/5843^k, where λ_ℓ = FG25 Def 3.14 theta element from Gross points on the definite algebra B_ℓ of discriminant ℓ·3·2243, Eichler level 5843·2^3·4547^2, paired with a mod-p^k level-raising eigenfunction g_ℓ. Required input: either a theta element / Gross-point evaluation on a definite algebra ramified at primes of N^- = 3·2243 and at ℓ, or an exceptional-zero derivative formula for λ_ℓ at the trivial anticyclotomic character (λ_ℓ(0) = c_0 = 0 by Lemma Λ1(a)). Manuscript content checked: ExactBSD §6-9 builds B_w as a BDP/Coleman-primitive measure on X_0(N) with ALL primes of N split in K and p split (06-pair.tex:3-9, 28-33) — no definite quaternion algebra, no level raising, no Gross points; the only definite-quaternion content in the family is Goldfeld2 §5 (05-coefficients.tex:242, 467) / Pointwise2 'coefficients.tex' (Jetchev–Kane reduction of Heegner points at a level-raising prime ℓ to Brandt-module coefficients), which is 2-adic (ℓ ≡ −1 mod 2^M), requires the Heegner hypothesis for K (fails for Q(sqrt-7)), and is itself a supersingular-point enumeration at level N·ℓ — the same ≈(ℓ−1)·2.7·10^14 scale the lab already classifies as UNAFFORDABLE (RETURN.md). No manuscript contains the words 'exceptional zero' in the BSD family. BREAK: no manuscript statement has the object λ_ℓ or any element of Λ/p^k attached to a definite algebra of discriminant containing primes of N, and no derivative formula at an exceptional zero.

Chain B (converse of FG25 Thm 3.4 via a full Heegner-point main conjecture, as FG Rem 3.5 suggests): would need equality of characteristic ideals for the bipartite Euler system κ_m / λ_m of FG25 §3 over K = Q(sqrt-7) with p = 5843 multiplicative and inert, N^- = 3·2243 definite side; plus a mod-p nonvanishing at the trivial character of the (exceptional-zero) anticyclotomic p-adic L-function or its derivative (the BCK input). Candidate manuscript theorem: ExactBSD Thm 9.6 ('U_w = B_w/L_w is a unit', i.e. equality of the strict Selmer determinant and the analytic series on Z_p[[t]]). Instantiation attempt: K := Q(sqrt-7), p := 5843. Hypotheses: Lemma 2.6(i) 'every prime dividing 2Np splits in K' — FALSE (3, 2243, 5843 inert; cf. SEED_CONTEXT line 36); 'p = w w̄ in K' — FALSE (5843 inert); 'analytic rank r ∈ {0,1}' of E — FALSE/unproved (ord ≥ 2 proved; K-A forbids assuming exactly 2 but either way ≠ 0,1); 'E(K) has rank one' — FALSE (rank 2). BREAK at the first hypothesis; even the companion construction (E^{D'} with a(E^{D'}) = 1 − r) is undefined for r ≥ 2. The same holds for TwoPrimary Prop 8.1 (needs s_2(E/K) = 1; seed has 2) and for Goldfeld2 Thm 3.3 / Pointwise2 Thm 4.2 (need corank 1 over a Heegner K).

Chain C (replace BLV Thm 7.3 'char_Λ X = (F F^ι)' in the G_bridge (reference/G_bridge_proof.tex (I2)) or supply the unit c_2(p) of the frozen route (07_good_primes.tex Thm B.3)): BLV's F is the anticyclotomic p-adic L-function of Gross points on the definite Shimura set of the algebra ramified at {3, 2243, 5843, ∞} (mass ≈ 5.4·10^14, Rem. m2cost), p good; ExactBSD's B_w is a Heegner-point (indefinite) measure requiring (H1)-(H3). No manuscript relates a definite Gross-point measure to an indefinite Heegner measure (no Jacquet–Langlands / Gross-point content in the BSD family). BREAK: wrong object and hypotheses (H1), (H3) fail.

Conceptual overlap only: the finite/singular switch s_loc(Z_{I∪ℓ}) = J f_loc(Z_I) at auxiliary inert ℓ (ExactBSD Lemma 6.8, TwoPrimary Prop 9.7 (K), Goldfeld2 Lemma 13.12, Pointwise2 Lemma 5.2) is the Kolyvagin/Howard Prop 1.7.4 derivative relation; the lab's bipartite system at 5843 already has the corresponding reciprocity laws from FG25 Thm 3.15/3.16 (loc_ℓ(κ_m) = λ_{mℓ}), used in Lemma Λ1 (NONZERO_B_THETA_CRITERION.md).
